programme_name: Spatiotemporal turnover of traits and biotic interactions
central_question: Do the same biological properties predict how rapidly phenotypic and interaction information is lost across evolutionary time and geographic space?
general_principle_under_test: Biological organization may be locally persistent without one universal global template; cross-system predictors can create coupling or decoupling between temporal and spatial turnover.
canonical_direction: All four primary responses are oriented so larger values mean faster turnover or faster loss of similarity with separation.

trait_time.label: trait temporal turnover
trait_time.separation: pairwise phylogenetic distance among focal taxa
trait_time.dissimilarity: predeclared trait dissimilarity among focal taxa
trait_time.minimum_within_system_support: at least 20 focal taxa with >=80% trait coverage and branch-length phylogeny

trait_space.label: trait spatial turnover
trait_space.unit: one biological radiation/system summarized from species-level spatial responses
trait_space.minimum_within_system_support: at least 5 focal species, each with >=40 georeferenced trait observations and nondegenerate spatial support

interaction_time.label: interaction temporal turnover
interaction_time.separation: pairwise phylogenetic distance among focal taxa
interaction_time.dissimilarity: Jensen-Shannon or source-appropriate dissimilarity of normalized partner profiles
interaction_time.minimum_within_system_support: at least 20 focal taxa with partner profiles, >=5 observed interactions per retained focal taxon, and branch-length phylogeny
interaction_time.opportunity_rule: partner availability/metaweb definition must be frozen before response calculation

interaction_space.label: interaction spatial turnover
interaction_space.separation: pairwise geographic distance among local networks
interaction_space.estimand: turnover_rho(geographic_distance, beta_os); report beta_st and beta_wn separately
interaction_space.minimum_within_system_support: at least 6 georeferenced local networks with aligned guild definitions and occurrence-aware species presence when available

abiotic_breadth.label: abiotic niche breadth
abiotic_breadth.measurement: pre-outcome occurrence-derived multivariate climatic breadth, standardized within taxonomic/guild frame
abiotic_breadth.forbidden_measurement: do not derive from the focal response trait or interaction turnover outcome
abiotic_breadth.interpretation: Broader abiotic tolerance should buffer state replacement across both axes if one common breadth mechanism operates.

biotic_specialization.label: biotic specialization
biotic_specialization.biological_role: dependence on a narrow partner/resource set
biotic_specialization.measurement: pre-outcome effective partner/resource breadth from an independent metaweb, training period, or external interaction source
biotic_specialization.forbidden_measurement: do not calculate specialization from the same local networks used to define the focal IS response unless a disjoint training split was frozen
biotic_specialization.interpretation: Specialization is a predeclared decoupler: it can conserve lineage-specific states through time yet increase sensitivity to local partner replacement in space.

mobility.label: mobility or dispersal capacity
mobility.measurement: guild-specific dispersal/mobility proxy frozen before outcomes and standardized within guild
mobility.forbidden_measurement: do not use observed focal spatial turnover as a mobility proxy
mobility.interpretation: Mobility is a spatial-decoupling control: strong spatial homogenization need not imply stronger evolutionary memory.

interaction_type_moderator.role: predeclared effect modifier, not a fourth predictor
interaction_type_moderator.primary_test: two-sided heterogeneity in predictor effects among interaction types
interaction_type_moderator.prior_art_note: Phylogenetic constraints have been reported to differ between antagonistic and mutualistic networks; no universal ordering is assumed here.

primary_cross_axis_tests.question: Does abiotic breadth affect trait turnover with the same sign in evolutionary time and geographic space?
primary_cross_axis_tests.success_rule: both standardized slopes have the frozen negative direction and the time-space slope contrast is estimable

primary_cross_axis_tests.question: Does abiotic breadth affect interaction turnover with the same sign in evolutionary time and geographic space?
primary_cross_axis_tests.success_rule: both standardized slopes have the frozen negative direction and the time-space slope contrast is estimable

primary_cross_axis_tests.question: Does biotic specialization decouple temporal retention from spatial turnover?
primary_cross_axis_tests.success_rule: temporal slopes are negative while spatial slopes are positive in the predeclared domain

primary_cross_axis_tests.question: Is mobility primarily a spatial homogenizer rather than a universal temporal-memory predictor?
primary_cross_axis_tests.success_rule: spatial slopes are negative; temporal slopes are reported without directional rescue

inference.response_standardization: within response type across independent systems before cross-response comparison
inference.system_dependence: one biological system/radiation is one independent unit; nested species, sites, years, trees, or sensitivity codings do not become independent systems
inference.model_family: multivariate system-level meta-regression with response-type-specific slopes and system random effect when data permit
inference.missing_cells: allowed, but direct time-space coupling for a domain requires systems measured on both corresponding responses
inference.no_global_score: do not collapse four responses into one universal turnover score unless a later pre-outcome identifiability test supports that reduction
inference.interaction_space_boundary: beta_os is primary for rewiring; beta_st is mandatory to distinguish rewiring from species replacement

admission_gates.gate0_source_identity: exact public source/version/file identity before biological response access
admission_gates.gate1_response_geometry: minimum within-system support and nondegenerate distance/dissimilarity geometry
admission_gates.gate2_predictor_independence: predictor measurement cannot reuse the focal response surface unless a disjoint training design was frozen
admission_gates.gate3_cross_axis_pairing: time-space coupling requires paired system identity, not unrelated pooled systems
admission_gates.gate4_known_truth_calibration: simulation must calibrate false-positive rate and detectability for the planned number of systems before confirmatory biological outcome opening
admission_gates.gate5_stop_rule: failed source/support/calibration gates terminate as HOLD; do not lower thresholds after outcomes are seen

proof_of_concept_only.CHUN: trait-time proof of concept for temporal memory and phenotype-resolution heterogeneity; not evidence for the general four-response law
proof_of_concept_only.FCP: trait-space proof of concept for spatial organization and non-universal global geography; not evidence for the general four-response law
